title: Entitlement bands & grace-scaling policy for Dedicated GPU reservations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Define and validate a new packaging primitive for Dedicated customers that combines (a) entitlement bands (soft reservation tiers) with (b) a short grace-window autoscaling policy and (c) a carryover burst credit mechanism. This ticket covers the product definition, experiment design, contract language for enterprise SQ, and handoff to pricing/commercial legal. Motivation: current reserved GPU contracts are all-or-nothing (hard capacity) which causes underutilized commit or expensive overage. We propose 'entitlement bands' (e.g., 50%, 75%, 100% committed tiers) where customers get guaranteed baseline throughput plus a defined burst envelope with preferential pricing and a short grace period to auto-scale while we provision dedicated capacity or fallback to compatible variants.
acceptance_criteria: Product spec drafted and reviewed by Eng, Sales, and Legal
Experiment plan with KPIs (rev uplift, net new committed capacity, churn delta, SLA adherence) approved
Contract/SQ language draft for enterprise legal and security questionnaire responses completed
Handoff ticket to Billing/Platform created for billing rules and telemetry events
Pilot cohort (3 customers) identified and comms plan ready
comments: 2025-02-14 — Aisha K: Kickoff — scoped as hybrid pricing primitive; shared initial hypothesis: entitlement bands reduce commit friction for mid-market and increase adoption in POC phase.

2025-02-21 — Liam O': Added initial pricing constructs: base reserved price = 0.7 * on-demand per-GPU rate at 100% band; 75% band = 0.83 *; 50% band = 0.92 *. Burst overage priced at 1.1 * on-demand for >band usage with carryover credit cap. Numbers are placeholders for modeling.

2025-02-25 — Eng (Marisol Chen): Feasibility note — runtime needs two changes: (1) grace-window autoscale (30–120s configurable) to warm additional pools, (2) tagging & telemetry for entitlement band usage and burst events. ENG-3821 to implement metrics; ENG-3950 to add autoscale policy hooks.

2025-02-28 — Sales (Diego Ramos): Suggested pilot customers: two SaaS companies (medium usage, strict latency) and one enterprise with seasonal spikes. Sales asked for >=95% baseline SLA on guaranteed capacity at band level.

2025-03-03 — Legal (Priya Menon): Drafted contract clause for entitlement bands, including termination rights, audit access, and clear definitions for "baseline", "burst", "grace-window". Requested to align breach remedies with existing SLA credit framework.
2025-03-05 — PM review (Aisha K): Updated experiment KPIs and added customer-impact matrix. Ready for cross-team review on 2025-03-07.

2025-03-06 — Design (Rafael Ortiz): Uploaded wireframes for billing UI exposure (Console) showing entitlement band selection, forecasted monthly spend, and burst credit meter. Need engineering to confirm feasibility for realtime burst meter.
2025-03-06 — Liam O': Noted blockers: dependencies on Billing API changes (BILL-112) and legal signoff on SQ language for 'data locality during burst'.
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Decided to offer three bands (50/75/100%) rather than continuous discount curve to simplify sales conversations and billing rules.
2025-02-21: Use short grace-window autoscale default = 60s with configurable range 30–180s; rationale: balance customer latency sensitivity vs provisioning cost.

2025-02-25: Burst pricing will be premium to on-demand to discourage unlimited usage; however pilot will include a small free carryover credit equal to 5% of monthly committed GPUs to demonstrate value.

2025-03-01: SLA credits apply only to baseline guaranteed capacity within chosen band; burst outages are subject to best-effort remediation and logging but not SLA credits. Legal to review customer-facing wording.
2025-03-04: Experiment will be A/B: cohort A (sales offering with 6-month commitment + band discounts), cohort B (control: standard reserved with identical price per GPU but no burst carryover).

2025-03-10: Engineering tickets (ENG-3821, ENG-3950) groomed and estimated; prioritize in Cycle 2025-W07
